text:
maya: Quick note — during the 02:00 deploy we observed tenant-A short requests piling up behind long seqs. p50 short latency jumped from 18ms -> 120ms, p95 to ~620ms. KV hit-rate stayed ~89% so not a cold-cache issue.

ton: Ugh. Which queue policy was active? Were we on fixed-window or adaptive-window?

maya: Fixed-window (20ms) with token targets tuned for overall throughput. The long lane monopolized the batch tokens.

liam: I replayed traces — long sequences accumulate and keep stealing batch slots because their token_budget > short_budget. The batcher coalesces aggressively (good throughput) but fairness is lost.

ana: @liam any idea on quick mitigations? Can we throttle long tails or add a short-priority boost?

liam: Two quick ideas: 1) window shrink when imbalance detected, 2) per-tenant short-priority credit refill with decay to prevent abuse.

maya: I prototyped a simple heuristic: if short_queue_len > long_queue_len * 2 then reduce window_ms by 50% for next 5 windows and give short lane +30 token boost. Preliminary run reduced short p95 to ~140ms.

ops-bot: Profiling dump: cpu@svc=0.21, gpu_busy=0.78, kernel_swap=0.05, avg_batch_size=11. -> indicates we still have headroom to run smaller more frequent micro-batches.

ton: Nice. Can you paste the heuristic config you used?

maya: Sure:
```
# adaptive window params
batcher.window_ms = 20
batcher.min_window_ms = 6
batcher.max_window_ms = 50
imbalance.threshold = 2.0   # short_queue_len / long_queue_len
imbalance.shrink_factor = 0.5
short_lane.token_boost = 30
short_boost.decay_seconds = 60
kv.priority_decay = 0.8   # reduce KV priority over time to avoid long-term hogging
```

liam: Two notes: 1) set min_window_ms > kernel_launch penalty threshold (we measured ~4ms overhead), so 6ms is safe. 2) token_boost must be budgeted globally or tenants may game it. Use a refill cap.

ana: Agree. For tenant-level fairness we should track a rolling credit ledger per-tenant and enforce an upper cap per minute. If a tenant hits cap, fall back to decline/queue.

ton: Any kernel-selection or KV changes needed? Kernel selection likes bigger batches — smaller windows may reduce kernel efficiency. Tradeoff.

maya: Right — we measured a ~4–6% throughput hit when moving to min_window_ms lots, but unit-latency improved for shorts. I think the cost is acceptable for PLG tiers; Dedicated customers could opt-in/out.

liam: Suggestion: dynamic kernel hints. When adaptive-window shrinks, force a different kernel path optimized for small batches / lower occupancy. That reduced throughput loss in the sim by ~2%.

ana: Action items:
- maya: push the adaptive-window toggle behind a feature-flag and add metrics for short/long queue sizes and per-tenant credits (due EOD).
- liam: prototype the kernel-hint switch and measure perf delta on staging (2 days).
- tony: add rate-limit cap to short_lane.token_boost in router (config + telemetry).

maya: I'll open the PR and add the config snippet and a simple dashboard.

ton: :+1: Please include an example of how this behaves under mixed ratio workloads (10% long -> 90% short, 50/50, etc.)

ops-bot: Reminder — link to previous starvation experiments: https://redwood.internal/notes/starvation-experiments (for context).

maya: Will do. If we can keep kernel hint + adaptive-window + per-tenant credit caps, we should avoid most short-request starvation without large throughput regressions.

liam: Sounds good. If we see tenants try to game short boosts, we can add a penalty multiplier that decays credit faster for repeat offenders.

ana: Ok — wrapping up. Thanks all.
